Tideglass
Terminal Docs About

What is this?

A whole Unix shell that runs on nothing but a browser tab.

Tideglass is a fictional product with very real code. It's a Unix-style command line — prompt, blinking cursor, history, tab completion — backed by a virtual filesystem that lives entirely in memory and persists to localStorage. There is no server. There is no backend to call. You open index.html over file:// and you get a shell.

A real filesystem

A tree of directories and files — a home dir, projects, logs, configs — seeded with believable content and mutated by actual commands.

Pipes & redirects

A hand-written parser tokenizes quotes, splits pipelines, and applies > / >> / <. grep, wc, sort and friends actually compose.

Line editing

History with ↑/↓ and Ctrl+R reverse search, Tab completion for commands and paths, and the readline keys (Ctrl+A/E/U/K/W).

Themes & CRT

Five color schemes (Harbor, Amber, Phosphor, Paper, Grape), adjustable font size, and a scanline CRT mode that politely disables itself if you prefer reduced motion.

Why "Tideglass"?

The seeded filesystem belongs to mara, who keeps a harbor's tide gauges talking to the modern world. Her main project, tidewatch, turns a crusty fixed-width serial protocol into clean JSON lines. There is a recurring 03:14 pressure spike on gauge #4 that she swears is not the tide. Poke around /home/mara and you'll find her notes, logs, and a lighthouse she keeps meaning to photograph.

It's a small world, but a complete one — the kind of thing that's genuinely awkward to build with page-builder blocks, and almost trivial with a few hundred lines of vanilla JavaScript.

How it actually works

  • fs.js — the virtual filesystem: a nested object literal expanded into live nodes, with resolve, glob, and mutations that persist to localStorage.
  • parser.js — tokenizes a line honoring single/double quotes, splits on pipes, pulls out redirections, and expands $VAR / $?.
  • commands.js — every command as a small pure-ish function that takes {argv, stdin, env} and returns {out, err, status}. Pipelines just thread stdin through.
  • shell.js — the terminal UI: the custom caret, scrollback, the readline-style editor, tab completion, the runner that wires redirects and pipes together, the tour, and the themes.
# count the markdown files under projects, for real:
find projects -name "*.md" | wc -l

# short-circuit: only cat if the dir change succeeds
cd projects/tidewatch && cat README.md | head -3

The fine print

  • VersionTideglass 1.4.0 "harborlight"
  • Runs onAny modern browser, including straight from file://
  • DependenciesNone. No frameworks, no build step, no CDN JavaScript.
  • DataStays in your browser's localStorage. Nothing leaves the tab.
  • Storage keystideglass.fs.v1, .env.v1, .history.v1, .prefs.v1
  • LicenseImaginary, but generous.
